span.label: A sparse signal can be reconstructed EXACTLY from a highly incomplete, randomly chosen set of its Fourier coefficients — with overwhelming probability — by solving an l1 (convex) minimization problem.

span.label: The recovery finds the object of minimal complexity agreeing with the observed frequency samples, provided the signal is sparse; the support-size condition is essentially sharp up to a log factor.

span.note: retracted: RE-GROUNDED. The published string was not verbatim in EITHER copy of the paper. A quote field promises the author's words; this held `Quotation withheld`. The verb `reconstruct f exactly` belongs to a DIFFERENT sentence, about recovering f from ALL its Fourier coefficients by the inversion formula. The paper's sparse-recovery claim uses `recover`, and the distinction between having every coefficient and having a subset is the paper's entire subject.
